Govt approves continuation of Stand-Up India scheme for 5 yrs udisha srivastav New Delhi, 11 November The Union Cabinet on Wednes- day approved the continuation of the Stand-Up India scheme for ﬁve years till March 31, 2031. The Cabinet, spearheaded by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, also approved a credit guar- antee corpus of ~4,111 crore to support lending under the scheme. The Stand-Up India scheme has set a target of ex- tending ﬁnancial assistance to at least 250,000 additional entrepreneurs from women, Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs). Launched in April 2016, the scheme has so far facilitated loans to more than 275,000 women, SC and ST entrepreneurs so far, according to the government. Under the scheme, eligible women and SC/ST entrepreneurs can avail loans ranging from above ~10 lakh to ~1 crore for setting up greenﬁeld enterprises. The loans can be structured as composite loans, covering both working capital and term loan requirements, or as term loans, and can cover up to 85 per cent of the project cost. The scheme covers enter- prises across manufacturing, services, trading and agricul- ture-allied activities. Under the scheme, the credit guar- antee coverage is set at 85 per cent of the loan amount, with a standard guarantee fee of 0.50 per cent. The continuation of the scheme is essentially aimed at improving access to institu- tional credit for entrepreneurs from underserved commu- nities and supporting the cre- ation of new enterprises.
